language_instruction: **Source language:** Classical (literary) Mongolian in the traditional Uighur-Mongol vertical script, printed from woodblocks (Beijing Kanjur, 1718–20). It is NOT Manchu. Columns run top to bottom and are read from LEFT to RIGHT. Transcribe in Mongolian script (Unicode U+1800 block), one source column per line, in reading order. The margin carries a Chinese section/volume/folio label. Report the primary language in the <language> tag.

ᠪᠣᠯᠲᠤᠭᠠᠢ ᠃ ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠴᠣᠭ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠃ ᠬᠤᠸᠠᠷᠠᠭ ᠡᠷᠳᠡᠨᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠦᠨᠡᠨ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ

<margin><term>Sa</term> <gloss>Tibetan letter used as the volume signature for Volume Twenty-Eight</gloss>, three hundred ninety-three, upper <note>recto, folio 393a</note></margin>
<margin><term>Zhupin jing</term> <gloss>Scriptures of Various Sections; original: "諸品經"</gloss>, Volume Twenty-Eight, upper <note>recto</note>, three hundred ninety-three</margin>
by that word of truth, unto me, and for the good fortune of all sentient beings,
may <term>öljei qutug</term> <gloss>auspiciousness and blessings</gloss> abide! The immaculate, timelessly transcendent
mind, and the radiance accomplished by its power:
the noble ones <note>the holy ones or saints, Sanskrit: ārya</note>, created by the splendor of merit,
who have thoroughly tamed the mind, and have reached
the furthest shore of all virtues, arisen through the power of truth,
perfected in good qualities; by that word of truth,
unto me, and for the good fortune of all sentient beings, may auspiciousness and blessings abide!
The <term>Ilaju tegüs nögčigsen</term> <gloss>Victoriously Passed Beyond, the Blessed One; Sanskrit: Bhagavān</gloss>, the <term>Tegünčilen iregsen</term> <gloss>Thus-Come One; Sanskrit: Tathāgata</gloss>, the Foe-Destroyer
<note>Sanskrit: Arhat</note>, the Truly and Completely Awakened <term>Burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>; perfected in virtues,
the Accomplisher of the Benefit of All Sentient Beings, the Knower of All
That Is to Be Known <note>the Omniscient One</note>, endowed with the ten powers <note>the ten cognitive powers of a Buddha</note>:
by that word of truth, unto me, and for the good fortune of all sentient beings,
may auspiciousness and blessings abide! The Verses of Auspiciousness are concluded.
In the language of India <note>Sanskrit</note>: <term>Radna traya suwasti gata</term> <gloss>Ratnatraya-svasti-gāthā, Verses of Auspiciousness of the Three Jewels</gloss>. In the language of Tibet:
<term>Gončog gsum gi bagrasis ki čigsu bčad ba</term> <gloss>dKon mchog gsum gyi bkra shis kyi tshigs su bcad pa, Verses of Auspiciousness of the Three Jewels</gloss>. In the language of Mongolia: Verses of Auspiciousness of the <term>Gurban Erdeni</term> <gloss>Three Jewels</gloss>.
I bow down to the Three Jewels. Supreme Great of the Great,
the Guide, God of Gods, Worthy Object of Offering, Savior of All:
by the word of truth of the Precious <term>Burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha Jewel</gloss>, may auspiciousness and blessings
abide! Deliverer from Evil Rebirths, Leading on the Path of Liberation:
by the word of truth of the Supreme Precious <term>Nom</term> <gloss>Dharma Jewel, the Buddhist teaching</gloss>, may auspiciousness and blessings
abide! Perfected in the Splendor of Merit: by the word of truth of the Precious <term>Quwarag</term> <gloss>Sangha Jewel, the monastic community</gloss>,
may auspiciousness and blessings abide! The Verses of Auspiciousness of the Three Jewels are concluded.
In the language of India <note>Sanskrit</note>: <term>Suwasti ayana gata</term> <gloss>Svastyayana-gāthā, Verses Leading to Auspiciousness</gloss>. In the language of
Tibet: <term>Bagrasis ki čigsu bčad ba</term> <gloss>bKra shis kyi tshigs su bcad pa, Verses of Auspiciousness</gloss>. In the language of Mongolia: <note>text continues on the next folio</note>

<summary>This folio from Volume 28 of the Mongolian Kanjur concludes a set of benedictory verses invoking the truth of the noble ones and the Buddha, presents the complete text of the Verses of Auspiciousness of the Three Jewels (Ratnatraya-svasti-gāthā), and opens the trilingual title heading for the Verses Leading to Auspiciousness (Svastyayana-gāthā).</summary>
<keywords>Mongolian Kanjur, Verses of Auspiciousness, Three Jewels, Ratnatraya-svasti-gatha, Svastyayana-gatha, Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, benediction, act of truth</keywords>
